notes.1a: (i) The majority of candidates were able to name the correct process.
notes.1aii: Many candidates found completing the word equation for photosynthesis challenging. A common error was to give the word equation for respiration.
notes.1iii: Some candidates found this question challenging. Some responses provided specific adaptations such as having a large surface area; others lacked detail, for example, stating that leaves were big which was insufficient.
notes.1b: (i) Most candidates were able to use the key successfully.
notes.1bii: Many candidates were able to produce a suitable sentence for the key. A common error was to create a question which gave the answer the wrong way round, e.g. they asked a question to which the answer was yes for leaf Fraxinus excelsior.
notes.2a: (i) This was well answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.2aii: While many candidates gave the correct response, some found this challenging.
notes.2iii: A few candidates were able to name the structure.
notes.2b: (i) Few responses correctly identified the coronary artery.
notes.2bii: There are many factors that can increase the risk of developing a blockage and most candidates provided good examples.
notes.2c: (i) Some candidates were able to identify the structure correctly.
notes.2cii: While some candidates were able to state the function of valves many found this question challenging.
notes.3: This proved to be a challenging question for some candidates.
notes.3a: (i) Some candidates were able to name the group correctly.
notes.3aii: Few candidates knew the sources of all three hormones.
notes.3iii: Some candidates were able to identify the relevant glands.
notes.3iv: Some candidates were able to state the functions of both hormones.
notes.3b: Some candidates were able to provide two effects.
notes.4a: (i) Some candidates could recall the definition specified in the syllabus.
notes.4b: (i) and (ii) Many candidates found this challenging. A few could recall the enzyme involved and the product of starch digestion.
notes.4c: (i) The majority of candidates correctly identified the structures. A common wrong answer was E.
notes.4cii: Some candidates correctly identified the structure. A common misconception was that absorption of food molecules occurs in the large intestine.
notes.4d: While some candidates gave correct responses. A number of responses did not answer the question asked and instead provided a description of ingestion. A common error was to state enzymes that are not active in the stomach.
notes.5: Many candidates were able to extract information and use graphical data accurately and this question was answered well by the majority of candidates.
notes.5a: (i) The majority of candidates were able to accurately extract data from the graph.
notes.5aii: The majority of candidates were able to calculate the time correctly.
notes.5iii: Some candidates were able to give two differences.
notes.5b: (i) Many candidates were able to recall part of the definition. Some responses were also able to make the link between the breakdown of nutrients and the release of energy.
notes.5bii: While many were able to state a useful product. Many stated alcohol which was in the question and was therefore not accepted.
notes.6a: (i) While some candidates gave a correct response many responses did not answer the question and it was possible that some had not read the introductory sentence that described the conditions in which the plant had been grown, i.e. in the dark.
notes.6b: (i) This proved challenging for many candidates, a few were able to give the correct stimulus.
notes.6bii: Some candidates knew the correct response.
notes.6c: (i) Again some candidates knew the correct response.
notes.6cii: While some candidates were able to provide a good response to this question, many found it challenging. A common error was to repeat the description given in the question and to omit the explanation as to why the shoots bent towards the light.
notes.7a: It was pleasing to see that many candidates answered this question well.
notes.7b: Candidates found this question challenging. A few candidates were able to successfully describe the stages involved in selective breeding. The best responses realised that sexual reproduction would be used in selective breeding, asexual reproduction. Some responses were less successful in applying their knowledge to a novel context.
notes.7c: This question proved to be challenging for most candidates. A few responses gave valid examples and successfully explained what genetic engineering is.
notes.7d: The majority of candidates were able to give suitable examples.
notes.8a: (i) Some candidates were able to put all of the statements into the correct sequence in the flow chart. Many found this challenging.
notes.8aii: A few candidates were able to state how new alleles are formed.
notes.8iii: Many were able to give features of mammals that are not visible. A common error was to give a feature that is common to all vertebrates rather than just mammals.
notes.8b: (i) The majority of candidates were able to define the term successfully.
notes.8bii: Many candidates were able to give two visible features. A common error was to give features that were not visible in Fig. 8.1.
notes.9a: This question was answered well by nearly all candidates.
notes.9b: (i) Many candidates gave correct structural differences. A common error was to give differences in function rather than structure.
notes.9bii: Nearly all candidates knew the purpose of a blood clot.
notes.key_messages:
Candidates should ensure that they understand the type of response required for command words such as
state, describe and explain.
notes.general_comments:
A good level of knowledge and understanding was seen for many syllabus topics.
Learning the definitions of key terms remains an important skill.
